records.region: West Greenland, inland-ice corridor east of Ilulissat and historical inner Jakobshavn Isfjord
records.candidate_name_role: No representative natural-river hydronym is supported for the complete inland-ice and inner-fjord composite.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The complete inland-ice and historical inner-fjord selection has no supported representative natural-river hydronym. Jakobshavn Isfjord names the receiving fjord only; mapped ice terrain and contours do not establish one natural river.
records.completion_scope: Completed ordinary selected geographic correspondence and null whole-natural-river naming determination; no registry verification or modern hydraulic investigation.
records.supported_name_scope: Jakobshavn Isfjord is supported only as a bounded historical receiving-fjord name. No whole-selection natural-river name is assigned.

scope_limits: Complete ordinary terrain and receiving-fjord correspondence does not establish a single continuous natural river. No representative natural-river hydronym is supported, and this does not assert that every local meltwater stream is officially unnamed.

Jakobshavn Isfjord is a bounded fjord name. The printed settlement label Ilulissat/Jakobshavn is only a geographic reference. Neither is promoted to a whole-feature river name, and no uninspected glacier-name alias is assigned.

The 1995 national compilation and private approximate orientation support ordinary-scale geography. They do not resolve exact present-day glacier-front, shoreline, bank or physical terminal status, nor modern flow behavior.

The supplied sea terminal class is preserved as metadata. The source and rendered positions are separately described in the historical inner-fjord setting; neither is a surveyed natural-river mouth, and the final rendered extension is not asserted to be a river channel.
No formal registry verification, Korean name, selected lake-throughflow, current surface/subglacial hydraulic route or surveyed river length is established.

bounded_name_observations.name: Jakobshavn Isfjord
bounded_name_observations.relationship: Name printed on the receiving fjord west of the lower Inland Ice. It describes the bounded inner-fjord approach and terminal context, not the whole modeled selection and not a river alias.

records.region: Texas; Little Prong–Buffalo Bayou, Barker Reservoir, Houston and Lynchburg–Brownwood receiving setting
records.geographic_disambiguation: Supported representative of the researched receiving system. It does not rename the separate Little Prong upper reach, reservoir, side tributaries or final San Jacinto/Brownwood receiving-water extension. No additional true alias was established.
records.completion_scope: Buffalo Bayou is supported as the representative receiving-system name for the complete selection. The chosen western opening includes separately named Little Prong, then joins Buffalo Bayou, passes through Barker Reservoir and Houston, and continues along the broad lower industrial channel into the Lynchburg–Brownwood receiving setting. Source and render terminals differ; the straight rendered ending is generalized across intervening land and is not an all-water mouth line. No material through-link remains pending at ordinary corridor scale.
records.supported_name_scope: Supported representative of the researched receiving system. It does not rename the separate Little Prong upper reach, reservoir, side tributaries or final San Jacinto/Brownwood receiving-water extension. No additional true alias was established.

scope_limits: The headmost minor connector is unnamed in the inspected maps; Little Prong applies only to the bounded mapped upper drainage.
The representative Buffalo Bayou name does not imply one natural-channel name for every reservoir, tributary, tidal-water or modeled extension component.
Ordinary mapped corridor and receiving-water correspondence is the scope. Current drainage operation, gate states, tidal direction, precise banks, waterlines and legal name boundaries are unverified.
The rendered final segment crosses land/shoreline near the terminal peninsula; separate source and render endpoints are retained. No all-water straight line or farther coastal mouth is claimed.
HCFCD profile corroborates the stream name only. Its linked studies, maps, diagrams and underlying cartographic inputs were not acquired or used.

records.region: Borden Peninsula, northern Baffin Island, Nunavut; Mala River valley and west shore of Navy Board Inlet
records.geographic_disambiguation: Researched Mala receiving system from the selected western feeder through the named incised valley and braided coastal plain. This does not give every feeder or individual terminal braid the same scalar name.
records.completion_scope: Mala River is supported as the representative receiving system. Independent imagery covers the selected western opening, northward canyon transfer, long eastward incised valley, side-valley joins, widening braided lower plain and actual coastal ending. Scotter’s own field prose locates the Mala valley within the selected lower-middle corridor, while CHS describes the river at Navy Board Inlet. All22stored parts are covered; the source and render sea endings remain distinct.
records.supported_name_scope: Researched Mala receiving system from the selected western feeder through the named incised valley and braided coastal plain. This does not give every feeder or individual terminal braid the same scalar name.

scope_limits: Formal name-registry status and Korean name remain unverified.
No exact upper hydronym boundary or claim that the entire selected composite bears one uniform scalar name.
The coastal selection follows the broader southern alluvial receiving floor; present wet-thread and exact modern mouth alignment are not asserted.
No absence of local or Indigenous names is inferred for selected feeder reaches.

bounded_name_observations.name: Mala River
bounded_name_observations.scope: Named lower-middle incised valley and coastal receiving system, supported by independent field prose and CHS coastal prose; representative identity does not rename all upper feeder reaches.

bounded_name_observations.name: Navy Board Inlet
bounded_name_observations.scope: Marine receiving inlet on the east side of the Borden Peninsula. Not an alias for the river.

records.region: Southeastern Ellesmere Island, Nunavut; Prince of Wales Icefield, Trinity Glacier and inner Talbot Inlet setting
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: A glacial terrain path with a bounded named glacier and marine receiving inlet does not establish one natural-river identity for the whole selected composite. Neither Trinity Glacier nor Talbot Inlet is promoted to a river name.
records.completion_scope: The complete selection is geographically established as an icefield–glacier–ice-covered marine receiving corridor, with Trinity Glacier supported only as the bounded lower glacial feature and Talbot Inlet as the receiving inlet. All31stored parts, ice-branch transfers and separate source/render endings are covered. No whole-feature natural-river name is supported, so the result is a completed null name-scope hold rather than a missing-source classification.
records.supported_name_scope: Trinity Glacier names the bounded lower outlet and Talbot Inlet its marine receiving setting. Neither name applies as a river hydronym to the complete icefield/glacier composite.

scope_limits: No natural-river hydronym is established for the complete icefield/glacier/marine composite.
Exact upper named-glacier limits and glacier-branch ownership are not established; named lower Trinity context does not rename the entire95.376km selection.
Present ice dynamics, subglacial flow, individual meltwater-pool status and exact modern front/grounding line remain outside the finding.
The separately stored source and rendered sea endings are both described at the broad ice-covered receiving-area scale; no exact current coastal endpoint is asserted.
Formal name-registry status and Korean name remain unverified.

bounded_name_observations.name: Prince of Wales Icefield
bounded_name_observations.scope: Regional icefield setting containing the selected western opening and outlet-glacier system. Not a river name.

bounded_name_observations.name: Trinity Glacier
bounded_name_observations.scope: Lower selected glacier corridor and marine-front setting identified by the study’s original figures and compared with independently read imagery. The named glacier does not rename every upper icefield branch or the sea-ice endpoint.

bounded_name_observations.name: Talbot Inlet
bounded_name_observations.scope: Ice-covered marine receiving setting beyond the lower glacier front. Distinct from the river category and from the neighboring Talbot Glacier.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
